questionSimple: Analia casts a kicked Rite of Replication targeting their Hamletback Goliath. After all triggers have resolved, what is the greatest total power that they could have among all of their creatures?
answerSimple: Probably 49,278. Analia chooses the order of the triggers on the stack. Each trigger checks the power of the creature that caused it to trigger when the trigger resolves, so the number of counters it puts on its source will be modified by any changes to that power while the trigger was on the stack. There are 15,511,210,043,330,985,984,000,000 different ways to order the triggers on the stack, so it's difficult to be certain of the maximum total power. The best that anyone has come up with though trial and error is 49,278, but the actual answer may be larger. If you're mathematically-inclined and would like to try to find a larger value, or prove that this is the largest, you can take a look at this StackExchange page to get started. (The difficult question is how to stack the triggers from the 5 that just entered, and the best that's been found for that is 24636 = 4106*6. Then to account for the one already on the battlefield, it's obviously optimal to resolve its triggers last, so we double that number and add 6 to get 49,278.)

questionSimple: Alex controls Alhammarret's Archive, Thought Reflection, Blood Scrivener, Lich, and Words of Worship. Nayeli controls Chains of Mephistopheles, Alms Collector and Rain of Gore. Neither player has any cards in hand. Alex activates Words of Worship once, then moves to their draw step. What is the greatest number of cards that Alex can end up with in their hand, assuming they make the best possible choices? What else happens in that scenario?
answerSimple:
At most Alex can end up with 29 cards in their hand. Rain of Gore only applies to life gained due to a spell or ability, not a turn-based action, so it won't apply to any life gain caused by Words of Worship. Whenever multiple replacement effects apply to an event (such as Alex drawing a card), the affected player will chose which one to apply first. Once a replacement effect has been applied to an event, it will not apply again to that event or any events contained inside that event.

* The event begins as "draw a card". * Alex chooses to apply Blood Scrivener's effect. The event is "Draw 2 cards, lose 1 life". * Alex must apply Alms Collector's effect. The event is "Draw a card, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex chooses to apply Words of Worship's effect to their draw. The event is "Gain 5 life, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex must apply Alhammarret's Archive's first effect to the life gain. The event is "Gain 10 life, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex must apply Lich's effect to the life gain. The event is "Draw 10 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex must apply Thought Reflection's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Draw 2 cards, draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex draws a card. The event is "Draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex chooses to apply Chains of Mephistopheles's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Discard a card, draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex discards a card. The event is "Draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex must apply Alhammarret's Archive's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Draw 2 cards, draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alex draws 2 cards. The event is "Draw 9 cards, Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * For the next 9 cards draws, Alex chooses to apply and perform Chains of Mephistopheles's effect followed by Alhammarret's Archive and Thought Reflection's effects, making them all "discard a card, draw 4 cards". The event is "Nayeli draws a card, lose 1 life". * Nayeli must apply Chains of Mephistopheles's effect to the card draw, putting a card from their library into their graveyard. * Alex loses 1 life.

Alex has 29 cards in their hand and 10 cards in their graveyard. Nayeli has 1 card in their graveyard. Alex has lost 1 life.

questionSimple: Azaria controls 3 Fire Elementals and a Viashino Bey enchanted with Errantry and Lust for War. Which creatures will Azaria need to declare as attackers when they goes to combat?
answerSimple:
The rules around attacking requirements are a little vague, but here's our best guess:

There are two requirements in this scenario: "If Viashino Bey attacks, all creatures you control attack if able" and "Viashino Bey attacks each combat if able". There is also one restriction "Viashino Bey can only attack alone".

If Viashino Bey is chosen as the only attacker, that satisfies the second requirement. It does not satisfy the first, since the Fire Elementals are able to attack, but aren't doing so. However it also satisfies the restriction.

If some combination of Fire Elementals are chosen as attackers and not Viashino Bey, the first requirement is being satisfied, but not the second. The restriction is being satisfied here as well. 

If no creatures are chosen as attackers, that also satisfies the first requirement but not the second. This also obeys the restriction.

In all cases there is one requirement being obeyed and one being broken, while satisfying the restriction. Any of them are therefore legal declarations of attack.

questionSimple: Ahmed controls Yarok, the Desecrated and casts Animate Dead enchanting their The Fugitive Doctor. What happens?
answerSimple: The first Animate Dead trigger resolves, bringing The Fugitive Doctor back to the battlefield, which triggers twice due to Animate Dead. When the second Animate Dead trigger resolves, it has already lost "enchant creature card in a graveyard", so that part of the trigger does nothing. It then gains another instance "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with Animate Dead." Then it attempts to return the enchanted object to the battlefield. It's unclear what this does to an object that's already on the battlefield. It certainly becomes a new object, as per [403.4]. (Which is also in line with [400.8] and [400.10]) But do enters-the-battlefield triggers trigger again? The CR doesn't specify either way, but the glossary entry for "enters the battlefield" implies that the answer is no. In either case, since the The Fugitive Doctor was put onto the battlefield with some instance of Animate Dead's ability, it satisfies both of its enchant abilities, so it remains attached.
